scope: Read all three complete final sources, eleven complete expanded declarations and all axiom reports, including the two-declaration even-index prerequisite. Checked three strict receipts and current source/object/log hashes against matching successful compiler receipts.
independence_disclosure: Parent authored the two SO2 consumers. Reviewer independently checked their finite-to-infinite composition and the imported even-index proof; no primary source in this review was authored by reviewer.
semantic_checks: The family includes every Cartesian degree n. Literal balanced support and degree n imply odd terms vanish and even terms are exactly the original x^(2m)y^0 coefficient times (x^2+y^2)^m, including all spectator factors.

The even-index embedding (m,gamma)->(2m,gamma) is injective. Off-image indices are proved odd and zero; unconditional HasSum is therefore transferred in both directions, without rearranging a merely conditionally convergent sequence.
Norm summability of the full original Cartesian family is derived from its exact even radial terms and zero odd terms. It is not assumed as a substitute for the required convergence proof.

The coefficient budget gives an actual analytic descended scalar sum on abs(w)<h^2 and supnorm(s)<h. This analytic statement does not need the polynomial homogeneity/balance hypotheses because it concerns the explicitly selected coefficient sequence alone.

The F identification assumes an actual Cartesian HasSum representation on its Cartesian polydisc. Uniqueness of HasSum compares this with the separately derived radial HasSum on the stated intersection; F=G(x^2+y^2,s) is not an equality premise.

For full descended bound M, every w admits a complex root x with x^2=w and abs(x)^2=abs(w)<h^2. Since h>0, abs(x)<h; the Cartesian point (x,0,s) lies in the original bounded domain. Pointwise identification then yields abs(G(w,s))<=M.

Square roots are used only pointwise after the actual descended sum has been proved analytic; no analytic square-root branch, derivative of a root at zero, or complex norm-squared substitution is used.
limits: The family P, its balanced support and coefficient bound, and the Cartesian HasSum representation hF remain explicit inputs. This does not yet derive them from an arbitrary physical function or from its real rotation invariance.
The identity is restricted to Cartesian abs(x),abs(y)<h together with abs(x^2+y^2)<h^2 and spectator domain. It does not extend that equality beyond its stated domain by assumption.

The M bound requires the explicit original function bound. Without it, only the prior geometric majorant bounds apply. Existing pinned Lean/mathlib caches are reused; no isolated dependency source rebuild or executable algorithm is claimed.
